earlier_scan.source_named: Burton, Scott Lynn 1996. A case study of lexical borrowing between language families: East Mindanao and Manobo languages (MA, UT Arlington) — comparative phonology plausibly covering Rajah Kabunsuwan Manobo; not online

sources.citation: Gieser, C. Richard (comp.). 1989. Bibliography of the Summer Institute of Linguistics Philippines 1953-1988. Manila: SIL. (archive.org djvu text)
sources.note: No entry for Rajah Kabunsuwan / Rajah Cabungsuan / Surigao Manobo -- no SIL Philippines work on this variety up to 1988.

sources.citation: Schumacher, Ron & Donna Schumacher. 1978. Proto-Manobo *l in Agusan Manobo. Studies in Philippine Linguistics 2(1):183-190. (closest sister language, agus1235)
sources.note: About Agusan Manobo, not mqk: sect. 6.3 p.189 'Stress is also phonemic in Agusan Manobo' with minimal pairs -- shows Zorc's/Lobel's areal 'Manobo lost contrastive accent' generalization cannot be transferred to East Manobo varieties such as mqk.

sources.citation: Gasing, Mae-Ann & Mohammad Ali Al-Saggaf. 2025. An archival study on the linguistic state of Obo Manobo and Kinamiging Manobo. Southeastern Philippines Journal of Research and Development 30(2):165-183.
sources.note: Mentions Manobo Rajah Kabunsuwan only in an Ethnologue-derived enumeration of Manobo languages and locations (pp.167-168); nothing on its phonology.
sources.venue: Southeastern Philippines Journal of Research and Development

sources.citation: Komisyon sa Wikang Filipino. 2023-2025. Repositoryo ng mga Wika at Kultura ng Pilipinas: Mga Wika ng Pilipinas (online language profiles, one page per language, based on KWF 'Lingguwistikong Etnograpiya' field documentation 2017-2021 and PSA 2020 census). Manila: KWF. Profiles read: 'Gáddang', 'Áyta Ambalá', 'Átta', 'Alangán Mangyán', 'Itnëg', 'Kalingga', 'Manóbo Agúsan' (all posted 5-6 Dec 2023).
sources.note: sociolinguistic profile only (location by barangay, vitality grade, PSA 2020 population/household counts, classification); no phonology, nothing on stress (diin)

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David, Jason W. Lobel & William Hall. n.d. [ms. c.2020-2022; published 2024 as ch. 7 'Historical linguistics of the Philippines' in A. Adelaar & A. Schapper (eds.), The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, OUP]. The History of the Philippine Languages. 44 pp. typescript, zorc.net item 142a.
sources.note: named only in the Manobo internal classification (after Elkins 1984); no phonology; accent is discussed only generically for 'accent-preserving Philippine languages' (sec. 5, ms p. 23)
sources.venue: The Oxford Guide to the Malayo-Polynesian Languages of Southeast Asia, OUP]

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason W. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa.
sources.note: Mentions Rajah Kabungsuwan Manobo only as having an angry register (p.207) and in two lexical citations (unap, mamang); no phonology of it. Areal remark p.287 fn.3: 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress' (not specific to mqk).

sources.citation: Gordon, Raymond G., Jr. (ed.) 2005. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 15th ed., entry 'Manobo, Rajah Kabunsuwan' [mqk]; also Lewis, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2014, 17th ed., and Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.) 2019, 22nd ed., same entry (full free web entries)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content: location (Lingig, Rajah Cabungsuan; SE Agusan del Sur; N Davao Oriental), population 7,560 (2000), intelligibility Dibabawon 80% / San Miguel Calatugan Agusan 81%, lexical similarity 82% Dibabawon, 76% Agusan; language use; no Typology line

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page raja1254 (Hammarström et al.), incl. reference list and 'Comments on subclassification: Burton, Scott Lynn 1996: 21'
sources.note: Nothing; only one reference (Zorc 1984, overview), Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; zero descriptive refs.

sources.citation: Grimes, Joseph E. 1988. Correlations between vocabulary similarity and intelligibility. Notes on Linguistics 41: 19-33. Dallas: SIL. (Table 1, rows B and P: 'Rajah Kabungsuan Manobo on San Miguel Calatugan Agusan' 76% similarity / 81% intelligibility; 'Rajah Kabungsuan Manobo on Dibabawon' 82% / 81%; data 'based on field surveys made by the Philippines Branch of the Summer Institute of Linguistics', via Ethnologue 10th ed. 1984)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: no phonology content (lexicostatistic and intelligibility percentages only)

sources.citation: SIL International - Philippines (collector not named). 1984-1990. Manobo, Rajah Kabungsoan wordlist [Expanded Philippine Word List (1966) in Rajah Kabungsoan Manobo, Lingig, Surigao del Sur; 372 lexical items; draft, neat and original versions]. SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 79693. Manila/Dallas: SIL. (OLAC oai:sil.org:79693; CC BY-NC-SA 3.0)
sources.note: No prose at all (cover notice + 9 scanned list pages, no symbol key). The transcriptions do mark word accent on most items: the handwritten original writes acute accents on vowels (tábak 'answer', ábu 'ashes', búta 'blind', útok 'brain', ságing 'banana', línas 'bark', mánok 'bird' vs. mapo-ít 'bitter', ma-itóm 'black', inúm, malisód, matignáw) and grave accents on some final vowels (tibò 'all', nabuyù 'anger', kaba-kabà 'butterfly', dagahà, malipà); the typed 'neat' copy renders the penult acutes as an apostrophe after the vowel (ta'bak, a'bu, bu'ta, u'tok, sa'ging). Both penultimate and fina…

sources.citation: Zorc, R. David. 1978. Proto-Philippine word accent: innovation or Proto-Hesperonesian retention? In Wurm & Carrington (eds.), SICAL Proceedings fasc. 1 (Pacific Linguistics C-61), 67-119.
sources.note: Areal/second-hand only: quotes Zorc 1977:298 fn.70 'Manobo languages (which have lost contrastive accent)' and sect. 4.5 'the Manobo group of Southern Philippine languages, none of which preserve contrastive accent' (examples Kagayanen, Obo, Tagabawa); Rajah Kabunsuwan Manobo not mentioned.

sources.citation: Elkins, Richard E. 1974. A Proto-Manobo word list. Oceanic Linguistics 13:601-641.
sources.note: Rajah Kabunsuwan Manobo not among the languages used (DIB stands in for East Manobo incl. Agusan dialects); no stress statement relevant to mqk.

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Agusan language' (redirect target of 'Rajah Kabunsuwan Manobo language')
sources.note: Nothing on stress; phonology section is Agusan Manobo consonants/vowels from Weaver & Weaver 1963; gives Rajah Kabunsuwan locations from Ethnologue and calls it a divergent variety.

sources.citation: Ethnologue, 'Manobo, Rajah Kabunsuwan' [mqk], public summary page (SIL International), downloaded via r.jina.ai
sources.note: Nothing; free summary only (status 'stable', Austronesian); full entry paywalled.archive.org connection refused).

sources.citation: OLAC resources page for mqk (language-archives.org/language/mqk); archive.org metadata and full-text search 'Kabunsuwan/Kabungsuwan Manobo'; UH ScholarSpace/Kaipuleohone search; Glottolog reference search (any field 'Kabunsuwan', titles 'East Mindanao', 'Surigao')
sources.note: OLAC page is now a JS app (no content retrievable); archive.org full text: 20 hits, all Ethnologue print editions, encyclopedias, acronym dictionaries, Wikipedia dumps; ScholarSpace: nothing; Glottolog: only Zorc 1984 and a genetics paper name the language.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed. Entry 'Manobo, Rajah Kabunsuwan' [mqk] (full entry incl. Dialects and Typology fields)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Full entry gives dialect/intelligibility notes and sometimes a Typology line; would confirm whether any description or survey underlies the entry. Older print editions (e.g. archive.org ethnologuelangua0000unse_k9t5, p.515) are controlled-lending only.

sources.citation: Burton, Scott Lynn. 1996. A case study of lexical borrowing between language families: the East Mindanao and Manobo languages. MA thesis, University of Texas at Arlington. xii+167 pp. (UMI 1382195; OCLC 702402976; MPI-EVA holds PDF)
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only linguistic work Glottolog ties to this language (cites p.21 for its subclassification); a comparative study of East Mindanao vs. Manobo languages that plausibly gives phoneme inventories/transcription conventions (incl. whether stress is marked) for Rajah Kabunsuwan Manobo.

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason W. field data on Rajah Kabungsuwan Manobo (angry-register and lexical elicitation underlying Lobel 2013 ch.6 and PSUB appendix), possibly deposited in Kaipuleohone (UH Manoa) Lobel collection
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Lobel elicited Rajah Kabungsuwan Manobo lexicon first-hand and marks stress with Tagalog-style diacritics throughout his work; his transcriptions would show whether stress position is contrastive in this variety.
